• References / citations UX: the answer-first layout is good, but the references section is hard to scan (entry 8).
• Note editing: you want to edit a note's title after saving (entry 8).
• Provenance detail: you want to see which notes were actually used to answer, not just cited IDs — the cited-versus-related distinction feels too subtle (entry 30, given as "Feedback on DeepNotes again", which suggests this is a refinement of earlier feedback rather than a first-time request).

Adjacent material that is NOT feedback, so treat it as context rather than critique:
• You own the domain deepnotes.dev and need to renew it before 12 October on the HDFC card (entry 7) — product context, not feedback.
• DeepNotes is your own college DBMS-for-personal-notes project with semantic (not just keyword) retrieval, built by a team of 2 (entry 18) — background, not feedback.
• An idea dump about layering spaced repetition / flashcards on note interpretations, with the risk that concepts are too broad (entry 29), and a draft tweet about a notes app forming opinions about your notes (entry 20) — these are product ideas in the neighborhood of DeepNotes, but they are not phrased as feedback on it.

So the recordable feedback is essentially two themes: reference/citation transparency and post-save editing.
